research_question: Does a universal HOT/WARM/COLD threshold exist for a capability across phase gaps, or do KEEP_WARM and FAULT_IN remain typed Pareto alternatives until an external price or hard constraint is supplied?

hosted_proxy.fault_in_method: best-effort POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED then file read plus SHA256 verification

primary_oracles: warm and fault-in return the same SHA256 digest
KEEP_WARM has zero requested transfer bytes
FAULT_IN has zero gap resident byte-seconds
for every positive phase gap, neither policy Pareto-dominates the other on the frozen typed vector
no scalar gain is emitted without an explicit external price vector
invariants: warm residency trades byte-time for lower requested transfer
fault-in trades transfer/resume work for lower gap residency
hosted file-read latency is a proxy, not a universal SSD law
no external price vector => no universal warm/cold winner
